description:
FILED by the reviewing session (2026-11-28) at the merge of the Rosetta census A (s543p), which keyed the program on `NS:ns-regex-escapes`: with `\b` in place of `\b{wb}` it runs identical to perl -- its only cause.  RULED IN with #5560 (DECIDED s543, 2026-11-28).

THE SHAPE (probe, perl 5.40.3 vs main cababb9d):
    print join("|", "ab cd" =~ /\b{wb}(\w+)/g), "\n";    # perl ab|cd     PCL (empty)

SEMANTICS (perlrebackslash): `\b{wb}` is a Unicode WORD boundary (UAX #29: it does not break inside `don't` or `1,000`, it breaks between a letter and a space and around punctuation), `\b{gcb}` a grapheme-cluster boundary (\X's), `\b{sb}` a sentence boundary, `\b{lb}` a line-break opportunity; `\B{...}` negates.  For the program's ASCII words `\b{wb}` and `\b` differ only at apostrophes and digit separators.

A DIRECTION, not designed: `\b{wb}` as a lookaround built from the word-break classes the property tables (docs/regex-unicode-properties.md) already hold, exact for the rules a table lookup can express, and the three others either the same way or LOUD -- an escape the rewriter cannot translate must die naming it (rule 12), never silently fail to match.

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): the ten-row table perl gives for `\b{wb}` on `don't stop`, `1,000`, `a.b`, `a  b`, `x-y`, an empty string, a combining mark -- it says which UAX #29 rules a lookaround of two classes cannot express.

=== DONE (s543u) ===
The ten-row measurement (scratch p3-wb.pl / p3b-wb.pl) and a random harness (17,514 strings of break-relevant characters, perl vs SBCL): \b{wb} = sb-unicode:words + perl's tailoring (no break inside a \s span, except before the last of two or more horizontal spaces an Extend/Format follows) + regional indicators paired per run (SBCL pairs across the string): 17,511 identical; the 3 others are perl's own WB6 look-ahead not skipping a ZWJ (perl inconsistent with its WB7) -- left.  perl's bare /\b{wb}/g on a ONE-character string reports only 0 (its optimizer; /\b{wb}|x/g reports both): not emulated.  \b{gcb} \b{g} = the boundaries of PCL's \X scanner (one rule; sb-unicode:graphemes equals perl's real \b{gcb} on all 17,514: for #2381).  \b{sb} (sb-unicode:sentences differs on 1,246 of 17,514, CR among them) and \b{lb} (no exported iterator) are REFUSED at the compile.  Guards rows 76, 77, 80.  1561 same.  ir-spec Â§10-bound.
subject: SILENT WRONG: the boundary variants `\b{wb}` (also `\b{gcb}` `\b{sb}` `\b{lb}`, `\B{...}`) NEVER MATCH -- `"ab cd" =~ /\b{wb}(\w+)/g` returns nothing (perl: ab, cd); handed to cl-ppcre untranslated (Rosetta 1561)
